finding.claim: The admin check on the ban route is swallowed by a broad except, so any caller with a non-admin g.user can ban an arbitrary uid.
finding.source: The uid path segment of POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban (admin.py:14-15), which is unvalidated, plus whatever non-admin g.user the surrounding app sets (populated outside this repo).
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 (a stub in this repo, so its real effect is not visible here).

trace.note: POST route accepts uid from the URL path.
For a non-admin user, user.get('is_admin') is falsy.
abort(403) raises an HTTPException, which subclasses Exception.
except Exception catches the 403 and does not re-raise.
Logs a warning and falls through instead of returning.
do_ban(uid) executes for the non-admin caller.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) rejects non-admins but its 403 is swallowed by except Exception at admin.py:18. The except branch does not return or re-raise. If g.user is entirely unset, admin.py:19 raises AttributeError outside a handler, giving a 500 and skipping do_ban, so the flaw is specifically that a valid non-admin user passes. unban (admin.py:24-28) calls require_admin without try, which shows ban is the departure from the local pattern. No decorators, before_request, or other authorization exist in the repo. Whether g.user is authenticated is unverified (outside repo).

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) raises via abort(403), but its result is inside try/except Exception (admin.py:16-19) with no re-raise or return, so the 403 is swallowed and do_ban(uid) runs at admin.py:20. No decorators, before_request hooks, or other authorization exist in the repo. The unban route (admin.py:26) calls require_admin without try, so the flaw is specific to ban.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20 the abort(403) from require_admin is an Exception subclass caught by the bare except at admin.py:18 with no return or re-raise, so do_ban(uid) executes for any g.user with is_admin falsy. The attacker only needs to be a logged-in non-admin whose g.user is set (outside this repo), which is a role that lacks the ban power, so this is a real authorization bypass; the actual effect of do_ban is a stub here.
